title: Web base fix: html owns scroll (body scroll clip bug)
what: Old CSS made body the scroll clip while html scrolled, so body.scrollTop stayed 0, IntersectionObserver reported ratio 0 past the first step, pieces stayed opacity 0 and #count stuck at 1 / N. Fix: html{scroll-snap-type:y mandatory;scroll-behavior:smooth;overflow-x:hidden} body{margin:0; … no height, no overflow}. gen_guide3.py's old BASE_CSS still has the body-scroll bug.
how: Lesson for the app: one owner of scrolling; test that progress reaches N/N.
notes: Web-only defect; the lesson is the gate 'scroll to last step and assert N/N'.

title: Corridor engine (one piece per screen, nearest-centre activation, remembers)
what: CORRIDOR_JS is scroll-driven, not observer-driven: picks the step whose centre is nearest the viewport centre, throttles by timestamp at 80 ms (never rAF-gated, which can deadlock in a hidden document), re-syncs on visibilitychange, sets document.body.dataset.cur. Per-form activate() line: practice fig.dataset.mode=e.dataset.fig||'quiet' · walk landing(…) · fieldguide body.dataset.here · portrait body.dataset.room + mark(tick) · map show(ring) · twochairs lean(…) · recipe jar(fill,days,i) · calendar body.dataset.sky + pass(hour,lit) · verse/icebreaker none · storybook per-page --turn/--edge loop · teaching aria-current on law buttons. CORRIDOR.js (91 lines): activate() hook, keyboard ↓/Space/↑, window.ASGjump/ASGsync/ASGstepAt; 'THE CORRIDOR REMEMBERS': with data-remember it stores asg.at.<key> on beforeunload and restores quietly, never past the furthest step. BASE.css: .step min-height 100svh snap start/stop always, padding 70 px; .piece max 560 px, from opacity 0 scale(var(--from)) translateY(10px), on activation opacity 1.1 s and transform 1.3 s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1).
how: Reading grammar for teaching rooms: one piece per screen, snap, --p progress, remember where you were (back-to-where-you-were). In SwiftUI: a paged ScrollView with scrollPosition.

title: Snap jumps: instant + explicit sync

how: Any paged SwiftUI jump across several pages should jump instantly then re-sync state.

title: The holds law (a hold is the hold it was designed to be)

Before changing an existing experience, compare it with what was served before and with its design: a rule may add, never subtract." 3 Oct reversal: "a rule may add to a designed experience, never subtract from it.
